title: Djokovic comes back as Sabalenka starts strongly in Beijing
summary:
Novak Djokovic had to work hard to keep his winning run going in Beijing. The six-time champion beat China's Bu Yunchaokete 4-6 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 to reach the third round of the China Open.

Bu won the first set. Djokovic then needed a medical timeout and spoke to a trainer while trying to regain his breath between points. He played strongly in the second-set tie-break. In tennis, a tie-break is a short contest used to decide a set when the players are level in games.

In the final set, Djokovic won four games in a row. A backhand winner ended the match after two hours and 52 minutes. The 39-year-old has never lost in Beijing across 31 matches.

Aryna Sabalenka also began her tournament with a win. She beat Mexico's Renata Zarazua 6-1 6-3 in 63 minutes. She hit 11 aces. In tennis, an ace is a serve that lands legally without the other player touching it.

Sabalenka lost her world number one ranking and US Open title to Elena Rybakina in September. She said expecting more from herself can drive her forward, but can also drain her energy.

Now ranked second, she is trying to be easier on herself. Her next opponent is Nikola Bartunkova, a 20-year-old Czech player who came close to beating her in June.
why_it_matters: The matches show two players advancing at the China Open. Sabalenka also describes how high expectations can motivate her while using up her energy.
